title: Catalysis and applying chemical principles
summary: Catalytic pathways, Arrhenius models, reversible relaxation and enzyme-rate derivation, with identifiability, inhibition and falsifiable experimental design.

objectives.description: Derive elementary reversible relaxation and distinguish its endpoint from timescale.
Use Arrhenius analysis within a tested temperature regime.
Derive the Michaelis–Menten initial-rate law with conservation and explicit approximations.
Test catalysis and inhibition claims using limiting cases, identifiability and controlled measurements.

preparation.description: Arrhenius slope in a constant-parameter regime

activities.title: Lecture notes and primary reading
activities.instructions: Work through the notes with the assigned source open. Reproduce each worked calculation or derivation on paper, including its assumptions, before reading the next step. Write one question that remains unresolved.

activities.title: Problem sheet: calculation, explanation and transfer
activities.instructions: Attempt the problems independently first. Use one hint at a time if useful, and record which help you used. Show the reasoning that connects the model and its assumptions to each answer; compare the reference only after a substantial attempt.

activities.title: Return without the notes
activities.instructions: On a later study day, close the notes and reconstruct the core relation and its assumptions, then explain the failure case from the last problem. Compare with your saved work and correct one gap. This practice does not itself certify mastery.

exitCheck.description: Use the whole problem sheet to judge the objectives: explain assumptions, complete the independent calculations and justify the final transfer/synthesis. The final exercise is the recorded checkpoint; its acceptance alone is not a claim that all course outcomes are mastered.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Catalysts change K because products appear faster.
commonMisconceptions.correction: At fixed conditions a new pathway changes kinetics; equilibrium for the same reaction is fixed by thermodynamics.

commonMisconceptions.claim: A steady ES concentration means the enzyme reaction is at equilibrium.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Quasi-steady intermediate abundance can coexist with continuing net product formation.

commonMisconceptions.claim: KM always measures pure substrate affinity.
commonMisconceptions.correction: KM=(k−1+k2)/k1 equals KD only with an additional rapid-equilibrium approximation.
